Sam — great to hear, and glad the demo landed. July 12 or 19 both work on our side. To make decisions quickly, can you confirm:

- Preferred date (12 or 19) and your timezone for invites
- Whether the session should be Americas-only or include EMEA observers (we'll add fallback times)
- Expected attendees and their roles (we'll match Redwoods: PM, Solutions Eng, Runtime Eng)

I attached a draft agenda and preflight checklist to this note (workshop-agenda-v1.pdf, preflight-checklist.xlsx). High level agenda highlights: 1) prompt review & best-practices (45m), 2) routing integration walk-through (45m), 3) live prompts and routing smoke tests (45m), 4) 45m load run and analysis, 5) action items/next steps.

Ben — can you confirm availability for July 12 and 19? KarThik / Dev — see load/run plan attached (loadtest-plan.md) and the sample prompts file (prompt-examples.json). We'll need DI/ETL support from Acme for the anonymized dataset (details in checklist).

Next step: once Sam confirms date + attendee list I'll send calendar invites with Zoom + the runbook link.

Thanks — Marissa

Quick technical notes for the pre-read and what we'll run during the session:

1) Prompt review: please include 10 representative prompts (we'll use prompt-examples.json). We'll validate token budgets and recommend quantization profile if needed.
2) Routing integration: Sam, do you have a simple endpoint we can hit to validate function/tool-calls? If not, we can scaffold a local echo endpoint.
3) Load test: aim for two phases — smoke (10 concurrent streams for 10m) then stress (200 concurrent streams for 20m). We'll capture latency percentiles and token-cost.
4) Data: anonymized sample must strip PII; please share S3 or a secure upload link.

Dev will prep a small harness and a k8s job to orchestrate the stress run. We'll include rollbacks and throttling pinned in the runbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
